evals.prompt: Add this as an insight on the site, this one's mine (Tom): [family office reporting cadence article, plain prose, no image, no explicit topic/date]
evals.expected_output: A new .md file in src/content/insights/ with author Tom Rutherford (role/image auto-filled from the known lookup), an inferred title/topic/excerpt/leadCaption, real word-count-based reading time, no image (leadImage omitted), one pull-quote and one subheading added to the plain-prose body, and order/featured renumbered across all six articles.
expectations: Article frontmatter sets author to 'Tom Rutherford', role to 'Family Office and Trust Advisor', and authorImg to '/tom-rutherford.jpg'
The read field reflects the real word count of the body at roughly 225 words/minute, not a stylized or copied guess
The body contains exactly one '### ' subheading
The body contains exactly one '> ' pull-quote, and its text does not appear verbatim elsewhere in the body
The body contains no markdown bold ('**') or italic emphasis markup
Across all article files, the order field forms a gapless sequence starting at 1 with no duplicates
Exactly one article file has featured: true, and it is the one with order: 1
All required frontmatter fields from src/content/config.ts are present with correct types

evals.prompt: here's a draft from shaan, can you get this onto the insights page. pasted from google docs so formatting might be a bit off. also attaching a photo for the lead image. [AI stack article with bold, H1 title, and a 3-item bullet list, plus an image attachment]
evals.expected_output: A new .md file with author Shaan Mahrotri, the supplied image placed in /public under the article's slug and set as leadImage, bold markup stripped from the body, the 3-item bullet list folded into flowing prose, the H1-style '# Why most...' heading treated as the title rather than rendered as a body heading, plus the usual frontmatter inference and order/featured renumbering.
expectations: Article frontmatter sets author to 'Shaan Mahrotri', role to 'Strategic Advisor and Operator', and authorImg to '/shaan-mahrotri.jpg'
The body contains no '**bold**' or '*italic*' markdown markup carried over from the source
The source's leading '# ' H1 line is used as the frontmatter title and does not also appear as a heading inside the body
The source's 3-item bullet list is folded into flowing prose rather than left as an unstyled markdown list
The attached image is placed under /public and the frontmatter leadImage field points at its actual path
Order/featured are renumbered across all existing articles consistently with the new article's position

evals.prompt: Got a longer one for the site, this should be dated August 2026. No author name in the draft itself, it's one of ours (Valora) — figure out who from context if you can, otherwise ask me. [co-investment diligence article, ~450 words, contains a 6-item diligence checklist embedded in a paragraph]
evals.expected_output: A new .md file with date 'August 2026' / dateShort 'Aug 26' taken from the user's explicit instruction, the skill either asking who the author is or making a reasonable Valora-context inference (flagged as a guess), a longer reading time reflecting the real ~450-word body, and the six-item diligence checklist flagged to the user as a structurally important list rather than silently folded or silently left as an unstyled list.
expectations: Frontmatter date is 'August 2026' and dateShort is 'Aug 26', matching the user's explicit instruction rather than defaulting to the current month
Since no byline was given, the output explicitly flags the chosen author as an assumption/guess to confirm, rather than stating it as settled fact
The 6-item diligence checklist is explicitly flagged to the user as a judgment call (list vs. prose) rather than silently converted either way
The read field reflects the real word count of the body at roughly 225 words/minute, not a heuristic like 'longer than existing articles so use a bigger number'
The body contains at most one '### ' subheading unless a second is explicitly justified by two genuinely distinct argumentative turns
